prompt.provenance_instruction: Answer the following question about Drosophila neuroscience. results.title: Brain region identification
results.question: What are the major subdivisions of the Drosophila mushroom body?
results.response: The major subdivisions of the Drosophila [mushroom body](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00004952 "Open mushroom body in Virtual Fly Brain") are the calyx, pedunculus, and mushroom body lobe system. This information comes from the Virtual Fly Brain database. According to the Virtual Fly Brain database, the mushroom body is divided into these three parts: the calyx, which receives sensory interneuron afferents, the pedunculus, a thick axon bundle extending from the calyx to the base of the lobes, and the mushroom body lobe system, which consists of a vertical branch and a medial branch. Virtual Fly Brain holds extensive data on the mushroom body, including neurons with some part in the mushroom body, neurons with synaptic terminals in the mushroom body, and images of neurons with some part in the mushroom body, among other data.

results.title: Neuron type classification
results.question: What types of Kenyon cells exist in the adult Drosophila brain?
results.response: The adult Drosophila brain contains several types of Kenyon cells, including alpha/beta Kenyon cells, alpha'/beta' Kenyon cells, and gamma Kenyon cells. These types are further subdivided into subtypes such as core, surface, posterior, anterior-posterior, middle, and dorsal, as stated in the literature (Lee et al., 1999; Aso et al., 2014). Specifically, the gamma Kenyon cells are known to innervate only the gamma lobe in the adult. VFB holds information on gamma Kenyon cells, including images, subclasses, expression patterns, scRNAseq data, and transgene expression.

According to the VFB database, these neurons feed reward or punishment information into the mushroom body. results.title: Neuroanatomy
results.question: What brain regions does the antennal lobe connect to?
results.response: The [antennal lobe](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003924 "Open antennal lobe in Virtual Fly Brain") connects to the mushroom body and lateral horn. This is based on information from the Virtual Fly Brain database, which states that any antennal lobe projection neuron sends synaptic output to the mushroom body, specifically the mushroom body calyx and/or lateral horn. Additionally, the [antennal lobe commissural pioneer interneuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003924 "Open antennal lobe commissural pioneer interneuron in Virtual Fly Brain") is not mentioned as a target of the antennal lobe connections in the available data. According to the Virtual Fly Brain database, the antennal lobe projection neuron term describes axons to higher brain centers, generally the mushroom body calyx and/or lateral horn. VFB holds data on 14 brain regions and over 5,000 neurons, including the antennal lobe and its connections.

results.title: Cell count
results.question: Approximately how many neurons are in the adult Drosophila central brain?
results.response:
The adult Drosophila central brain contains approximately more than 125,000 neurons, according to the Virtual Fly Brain database, as retrieved from VFB. 

VFB also holds data on the [adult central brain astrocyte-like glial cell](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00047885 "Open adult central brain astrocyte-like glial cell in Virtual Fly Brain"), including [2](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00047885,SubclassesOf "Run in VFB: Subclasses of adult central brain astrocyte-like glial cell") subclasses and [3](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00047885,TransgeneExpressionHere "Run in VFB: Transgene expression in adult central brain astrocyte-like glial cell") records of transgene expression.

results.response:
The main components of the [adult central complex](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00004913 "Open adult central complex in Virtual Fly Brain") include the ellipsoid body, the fan-shaped body, the three paired noduli, the asymmetrical bodies, and the protocerebral bridge (vfb). These components are associated with various functions, although the specific functions are not detailed in the available evidence. 

VFB holds a range of data related to the adult central complex, including images, neuron information, parts of the adult central complex, and transgene expression data. results.title: Circuit motif

results.response:
The dopaminergic input to [mushroom body](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00047953 "Open mushroom body in Virtual Fly Brain") output neurons (MBONs) comes from various types of dopaminergic neurons, including adult dopaminergic mushroom body input neurons and adult dopaminergic PAM neurons, as well as specific DAN types such as dopaminergic PPL1 neurons and dopaminergic PAM neurons (literature, as found in VFB). 

VFB holds information on the connectivity partners of MBONs, with 77 upstream class-connectivity partners matching "dopaminergic neuron" for MBON, including adult dopaminergic mushroom body input neuron, adult dopaminergic PAM neuron, dopaminergic PPL1 neuron, dopaminergic PAM neuron 6, and dopaminergic PAM neuron 8 (vfb, from the "VFB found 77 upstream class-connectivity partners" query). 

Specifically, the top mapped pairs include adult dopaminergic mushroom body input neuron to adult [mushroom body output neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00047953 "Open mushroom body output neuron in Virtual Fly Brain") (vfb). 

VFB also has extensive data on the mushroom body, including neurons with some part in the mushroom body ([602](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00047953,NeuronsPartHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with some part in mushroom body") records), neurons with synaptic terminals in the mushroom body ([599](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00047953,NeuronsSynaptic "Run in VFB: Neurons with synaptic terminals in mushroom body") records), and images of neurons with some part in the mushroom body ([22137](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00047953,ImagesNeurons "Run in VFB: Images of neurons with some part in mushroom body") records) (VFB data).

results.title: Neuron characterisation
results.question: What is known about the LPLC2 visual neuron type? Where is it, what does it connect to, and what is its function?
results.response: The [LPLC2](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/VFB_jrch0fva "Open LPLC2 in Virtual Fly Brain") visual neuron type has the ID [1813403998](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/VFB_jrch0fva "Open 1813403998 in Virtual Fly Brain"). It is a lobula plate-lobula columnar neuron, with a distinct dendritic arbor in each lobula plate layer. The dendritic arbor extends outwards from the main fiber in the direction of motion detection for the layer. LPLC2 detects looming, or expansion, stimuli. This neuron type has connections to various neurons, including adult cholinergic neurons, T5c neurons, and transmedullary neurons. VFB holds information on 1813403998, including its neuron profile and connections.

results.title: Pathway tracing
results.question: Trace a pathway from olfactory receptor neurons to the lateral horn. What are the intermediate neuron types and their connections?

The connections between these neurons can be described as follows: olfactory receptor neurons (ORN) -> antennal lobe projection neuron -> lateral horn. 

VFB holds a significant amount of data related to the [adult lateral horn](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00007053 "Open adult lateral horn in Virtual Fly Brain"), including images, neurons with various types of terminals, tracts/nerves innervating it, lineage clones, and transgene expression data. results.title: Anatomical containment chain
results.question: Trace the anatomical containment hierarchy from the DA1 glomerulus up to the top-level brain structure. What is each level in the hierarchy?
results.response:
The anatomical containment hierarchy from the [antennal lobe glomerulus DA1](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003932 "Open antennal lobe glomerulus DA1 in Virtual Fly Brain") up to the top-level brain structure is: antennal lobe glomerulus DA1 -> adult olfactory antennal lobe glomerulus -> adult antennal lobe -> adult deutocerebrum -> adult cerebrum -> adult central brain -> adult brain. This information comes from the Virtual Fly Brain database, which describes the parent-child relationships between these brain structures. 

According to the Virtual Fly Brain database, the antennal lobe glomerulus DA1 is a type of adult olfactory antennal lobe glomerulus, which is part of the adult antennal lobe. The adult antennal lobe is part of the adult deutocerebrum, which is part of the adult cerebrum. The adult cerebrum is part of the adult central brain, and the adult central brain is part of the adult brain.

Virtual Fly Brain holds data on neurons and images related to the antennal lobe glomerulus DA1, including [10](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00003932,NeuronsPartHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with some part in antennal lobe glomerulus DA1") neurons with some part in antennal lobe glomerulus DA1, [911](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00003932,ImagesNeurons "Run in VFB: Images of neurons with some part in antennal lobe glomerulus DA1") images of neurons with some part in antennal lobe glomerulus DA1, and transgene expression data in antennal lobe glomerulus DA1.

results.title: Complete neuron profile
results.question: Give me a comprehensive profile of the giant fiber neuron: its anatomy, connectivity, available driver lines, and relevant publications.
results.response:
The [giant fiber neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00004020 "Open giant fiber neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), also referred to as [DNp01](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00004020 "Open DNp01 in Virtual Fly Brain"), is a large adult descending neuron that controls jump escape behavior. Its distinct anatomy includes a large cell body located posterior to the lower protocerebrum and a large descending axon that enters the cervical connective via the posterior cerebro-cervical fascicle (Thomas and Wyman, 1984; Koto et al., 1981). The giant fiber neuron arborizes in the ipsilateral zones A and B of the antennal mechanosensory and motor center. There is one giant fiber neuron per hemisphere (Koto et al., 1981; Namiki et al., 2018; Sturner et al., 2025). 

In terms of connectivity, VFB holds downstream connectivity classes for DNp01 ([361](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,DownstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Downstream connectivity classes for DNp01") records) and upstream connectivity classes for DNp01 ([435](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,UpstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Upstream connectivity classes for DNp01") records), indicating the complexity of its connections within the Drosophila nervous system. 

For experimental manipulation, there are available driver lines, as evidenced by the [14](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,TransgeneExpressionHere "Run in VFB: Transgene expression in DNp01") records of transgene expression in DNp01 held by VFB. Additionally, VFB has [22](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,ListAllAvailableImages "Run in VFB: List all available images of DNp01") images of DNp01, which can be useful for understanding its anatomy and morphology.

Relevant publications include those by Thomas and Wyman (1984), Koto et al. (1981), Namiki et al. (2018), and Sturner et al. (2025), which provide insights into the giant fiber neuron's role in jump escape behavior and its anatomical characteristics. The giant fiber neuron's ID is FBbt_00004020, as per the VFB database.

results.title: Comparative analysis
results.question: Compare the downstream targets of the two main types of clock neurons (s-LNv and l-LNv). Do they converge on any common target neuron types?
results.response:

results.question: What is the connectivity between thermosensory neurons and the mushroom body? Could temperature information influence memory formation?
results.response:
The connectivity between thermosensory neurons and the [mushroom body](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00005801 "Open mushroom body in Virtual Fly Brain") is such that thermosensory projection neurons relay temperature-detecting neurons to higher brain centers, including mushroom-body-associated dopaminergic neurons and gamma main Kenyon cells, as indicated by VFB downstream class-connectivity previews for adult thermosensory projection neurons. 

The mushroom body itself is involved in olfactory associative learning and memory, and it receives sensory interneuron afferents to the calyx and neurons with presynaptic terminals in the mushroom body, according to the VFB mushroom body description. 

Given that thermosensory projection neurons can relay information to the mushroom body, it is possible that temperature information could influence memory formation, as the mushroom body is known to be involved in associative learning and memory. 

VFB holds a substantial amount of data related to the mushroom body, including [602](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00047228,NeuronsPartHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with some part in mushroom body") neurons with some part in the mushroom body, [367](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00047228,NeuronsPresynapticHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with presynaptic terminals in mushroom body") neurons with presynaptic terminals in the mushroom body, and [23](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00047228,ExpressionOverlapsHere "Run in VFB: Expression patterns overlapping mushroom body") expression patterns overlapping the mushroom body, which could be used to further investigate the relationship between thermosensory neurons and the mushroom body.
